answer: Each candidate identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the endpoint cheaply. Because one chain is sequential, GPUs cannot split that identity’s work into parallel steps, imposing a physical time cost. An attacker may run clone chains concurrently, but must spend additional compute for each, so summit, onyx, and sparrow identities cannot be created instantly at negligible cost.
